questions.q: How does a table get divided into micro-partitions in Snowflake?
options: Micro-partitions must be created one at a time with INSERT INTO PARTITION
By manually running CREATE PARTITION FUNCTION, as in SQL Server
Only if the table owner explicitly enables partitioning
Automatically, the moment data lands in the table — no partition key is chosen by the user
questions.explain: Unlike SQL Server's manual partition function and scheme, Snowflake automatically divides every table into micro-partitions as data loads — there is no key to design.

questions.q: Roughly how large is a single micro-partition (uncompressed)?
options: Exactly 1 GB, always
10 TB
1-2 KB
questions.explain: Micro-partitions are contiguous, immutable units of storage, each holding roughly 50-500 MB of uncompressed data (about 8-16 MB compressed on disk).

questions.q: What metadata does Snowflake's cloud services layer keep for each micro-partition?
options: A full copy of every row, duplicated for backup
The name of the user who last queried it
Nothing — micro-partitions carry no metadata at all
The minimum and maximum value of each column within it
questions.explain: Snowflake tracks per-column min/max metadata for every micro-partition, stored separately from the data and cheap to check without touching warehouse compute.

questions.q: What does partition pruning actually do?
options: Compresses a micro-partition's data further to save space
Permanently deletes old micro-partitions to save storage
Merges small micro-partitions into larger ones automatically
Skips micro-partitions whose min/max metadata can't possibly match a query's filter, before scanning any data
questions.explain: Pruning checks each micro-partition's min/max metadata against a query's filter and skips any partition whose range can't contain a match, scanning only what's left.

questions.q: What does SYSTEM$CLUSTERING_INFORMATION's average_depth value tell you?
options: The exact dollar cost of the table's storage
The number of rows in the table
How many users have access to the table
Roughly how well-clustered a column already is, which relates to pruning potential
questions.explain: average_depth is a clustering-quality metric — lower generally means the column's values are more naturally grouped together across fewer micro-partitions, which helps pruning.
